experiment: #8 baselines vs the real d=42 UNSW-NB15 surrogate, RECALIBRATED gamma=2.3061. Decision #2: re-run adv-training, input-smoothing, and Chen et al. query-blinding for REAL against the real surrogate (not placeholders), then FFI transfer-validate (mirror #7).
protocol: shadow/run_baselines.py. For each baseline, the attack harness differentiates through the baseline's OWN defended forward (exact parallel to the MIDAS rotation defense): PGD (L-inf eps=0.1, alpha=0.01, T=50) and C&W-L2 (iters=100, c_steps=3, initial_c=1, lr=0.01). naive attacker = ignores the differentiable-expectation/rotation (for input_smoothing: attacks base classifier directly; structurally naive==adaptive for chen/blinding given no rotational manifold parameter). ASR = fraction of n=200 benign-subset samples (nat_conf<=0.95) whose defended prediction flips vs natural label; defense-success = 1 - ASR. Baselines have no coupled-basis manifold rotation, so evaluated on the input-space attack only.

input_smoothing.desc: Gaussian input smoothing, sigma=0.1, K=32 MC expectation (SmoothedClassifier)

chen_query_blinding.desc: Chen et al. query-blinding / classifier rejection (reject if natural confidence < tau=0.75); naive==adaptive structurally

adv_training.desc: Madry-style min-max adversarial training (PGD T=10, eps=0.1 augmentation every 5th epoch), retrained surrogate; naive==adaptive structurally

headline_honest_findings.input_smoothing_vs_adaptive_pgd: Plain input smoothing (sigma=0.1) is essentially defeated by the adaptive PGD attacker on this d=42 surrogate (defense-success 0.000) -- the attacker differentiates through the MC expectation. It DOES block C&W (0.825-1.000) because C&W's L2 budget cannot push through the noisy expectation.
headline_honest_findings.chen_query_blinding: Moderate vs PGD (0.485-0.510), strong vs C&W (0.945) -- tau=0.75 rejection defends most C&W because C&W's minimal L2 perturbations land near the boundary / stay low-confidence.
headline_honest_findings.adv_training_is_strongest: Adversarial training is the strongest baseline vs PGD (0.705-0.710) and solid vs C&W (0.840). Still falls below MIDAS-Edge's reported attacker-coupled adaptive edge (see defense_success_rate_pi.json) and has no per-query detection signal.
headline_honest_findings.baseline_significance: These are REAL measured surrogate-side defense-success numbers, replacing the placeholder stubs that were previously in report.rs. Each baseline is also FFI-transfer-validated (#7-mirror) so the surrogate-side robustness is checked against the deployed TFLite model.

ffi_transfer_validation_production_tflit.protocol: #7-mirror: per-baseline naive+adaptive PGD (T=50 eps=0.1) batches classified by the production FFI float32 TFLite classifier (classify_transfer). ASR = flip-rate vs surrogate natural label on the deployed model.
ffi_transfer_validation_production_tflit.finding: adv_training robustness transfers best to the deployed classifier (0.345-0.38 ASR); input_smoothing transfers worst (adaptive 1.000) -- its surrogate-side weakness is confirmed on the real model; chen in between (0.685-0.71).
